Under development and roadmap

What is built, what is being built, and what comes next, stage by stage. Taken from the build roadmap of the app (updated 2026-11-12) and of the website (updated 2026-11-05).

M0 Foundation — E1 app

4 of 4 stages done

The application as it runs today: projects, 2D sheets with P&ID symbols and lines, attributes, history and undo, floating windows, and Alex in the chat. Every action is one command, used the same way by the interface, Alex, and outside agents, with a local-first AI policy.

StageWhatStatusWhat you can try
R1-5Refactoring: tests, one domain model, server modules, migrations, the server as the only writerDoneThe code was restructured and covered by tests. The app looks and works as before.
R-FFollow-up: per-user state, frontend structure, typesDonePer-user state and code structure. Nothing new on screen.
6A-6HOne command registry, safe AI edits, local-first AIDone 2026-11-02In the chat, check the mode chip in the header, ask Alex (Agent) to change a sheet, and use Undo on its reply (or turn on "Review changes first" and use Apply / Discard).
6IParity tests, enforcement, and the evaluation set for AI modelsDone 2026-11-02Tests that the interface, Alex, and outside agents run the same commands. Nothing new on screen.

M1 Object model — E1 app

11 of 11 stages doneMVP

Every engineering thing becomes one object with one owner, a class from a versioned library, attributes with sub-attributes and units, and typed relationships to other objects across sections. The library defines how objects behave (where they may live, what they may contain and relate to), and every tool follows the same rules. Tags come from the project's own naming rules. Today's symbols move into signed content packages as records, and every command works object by object, ready for the database of M2.

M1.0bTest automation pipeline (CI)Done 2026-11-02Every test now runs automatically on each change (GitHub Actions). Nothing new in the app.
M1.1Content packages and the libraryDone 2026-11-02The symbols now come from signed content packages. The symbol picker and the sheets look exactly as before; asking Alex which symbols exist gives the same list.
M1.1bSymbols as content package records, drawn by one renderer (formerly M1.9)Done 2026-11-02Nothing should look different: every symbol is now drawn from its record in the content packages. Open Insert > Asset and page through the types, place a few symbols on a sheet and connect them, and open Model Space: all should look exactly as before.
M1.2Record-level store and the object model migrationDone 2026-11-02Mostly under the hood. Open an existing project: the tree, sheets, and History should look as before, and every edit (and Alex) should still work.
M1.3Content packages visible in project settingsDone 2026-11-02Select a project and choose File > Project settings: its content packages (Core, Electrical foundation, and Plant engineering, which includes instrumentation & control) are listed with versions and what requires each. Ask Alex which content packages the project uses, or what you can place from Plant.

M1.6Relationships between objectsDone 2026-11-02Create a function under Systems (New system…), and on its Relationships tab choose "is implemented by", pick a pump in the tree and Add: the pump shows under the function. Or drag the pump onto the function with the right mouse button.
M1.7Tags and reference designationsDone 2026-11-02Create a few pumps under Assets without a name: they become P-001, P-002 with the designation -P. Change a pump's short code and see its tag marked out of date; right-click it, Tag…, type a manual tag; then More (…) > Retag… with the preview.
M1.8Tag configuratorDone 2026-11-02Open File > Project settings: under Tag rules, add a rule for pumps (text PU, then the number from 101), watch the sample, Test against project, Save rules, then create a pump under Assets and see it tagged PU-101.

M2 Platform — E1 app

9 of 9 stages doneMVP

E1 moves onto PostgreSQL and into the vendor's cloud. People sign in, belong to organizations, and are invited to projects with roles down to a single section or drawing. Two engineers can work in the same project at the same time without overwriting each other, Alex's proposals are kept safely on the server, and the technical security baseline is in place.

StageWhatStatusWhat you can try
M2.1PostgreSQL store with the object and history tablesDone 2026-11-03Behind the scenes: with npm run db:up, db:migrate, and db:seed, then E1_STORE=postgres, projects open and edit as before, stored in PostgreSQL tables that keep each organization apart.
M2.2Accounts and sign-inDone 2026-11-03Start npm run dev:identity and the server with E1_AUTH=oidc (README): the sign-in screen appears; the first sign-in claims the installation, a second email gets its own empty workspace.
M2.3Import of existing workspacesDone 2026-11-03Run npm run db:import -- data/db.json, start the server on PostgreSQL, and open it: the tree, sheets, history, and your chat are all there.
M2.4Organizations, invitations, and license tablesDone 2026-11-03On the server with sign-in on, open File > Organization…, invite a colleague by email, open the link signed in as them, and see them listed with their license and the seats used.
M2.5Project permissionsDone 2026-11-03Open a project and choose Members: give a colleague Reviewer; signed in as them, the project opens but moving a symbol is refused with the permission it needs.
M2.6Live refresh, safe saves per object, and stored proposalsDone 2026-11-03Sign in as two people on one project in two browsers: a rename in one appears in the other without reloading; a reply held for review is still there to apply after the server restarts.
M2.7File storageDone 2026-11-03On the server, attach a file to a chat message or upload one to a project, reload the page, and open it again; signed in as someone without a role in the project, it is not found.
M2.8Reference cloud deploymentDone 2026-11-06Open https://app.lanxtor.com in a normal browser, without installing anything, and sign in: the status bar (bottom right) says Microsoft Azure.
M2.9Technical security baseline and the M2 gateDone 2026-11-04Mostly under the hood: security settings and checks. You may notice session timeouts and stricter sign-in rules.

M3 Lists and connectivity — E1 app

12 of 12 stages doneMVP

Pipes, cables, wires, and signals become objects connected to ports. Any list is a live table of the model: right-click any node, Query ▸ New query… lists every object below it, in an Excel-like query view that can be filtered, edited, saved as a template (then listed under Query ▸), and exported to Excel. There are no fixed lists. The large 2D drawing editor arrives here. After M3, a first informal pilot preview.

M4 Documents — E1 app

31 of 35 stages doneMVP

Datasheets designed by the users: each object has its datasheet, where values are viewed and edited, and the same layout prints. Documents with revisions and issues, PDF of 2D spaces, lists, and datasheets with a title block, Excel import, search, object history, comments, tasks, generated loop diagrams, Alex's engineering patterns, redlining (markups on a 2D space, review rounds, marked-up prints), specification attributes for instruments, and document control (versions and revisions on the sheet, changes since a date, clouds in outputs). Everyone sees who else has the same sheet open (presence; no live pointers). M4 ends with pilot readiness: access control first (permissions by category, custom roles, who sees what, objects assigned to a person or group, an exportable access history), then a second cloud, billing, a signed desktop app, passkeys, and the security and legal reviews a pilot partner needs.

M5 Library lifecycle — E1 app

27 of 28 stages doneMVP

Companies edit and publish their own library: classes, attributes, relationship types, and how they behave. Projects see which updates are available and upgrade with a preview. Equipment catalogs with manufacturer data, a symbol designer with SVG import and live attribute labels, units of measurement, switching, licensing, and updates of content packages, specification datasheets (components, cases, templates inspired by ISA 20 and API), and document control's sheet templates, sign-off routes, reports and filing.

11.2Updates available, checked against projectsDone 2026-11-05Configuration → Company library: publish a second version of a company class; Updates available in this project lists its objects still on version 1 and what changed.
